\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-103},
  title = {The error alert judges a window against its countries' test MdAPE},
  date = {2026-11-07},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Monitoring, Model Evaluation},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (options, analysis, implementation)},
  decision = {ModelErrorHigh compares a window's MdAPE with the test MdAPE of its countries in \texttt{segments.\allowbreak{}csv}, weighted by its labelled answers, and fires above 1 + 3.55 sqrt(1 / n + 1 / m) times it, m the test rows of that baseline.
A country with fewer than 500 test rows takes the overall value.
ModelCoverageLow keeps the nominal 90\,\% floor.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item The overall test MdAPE (EDN-101): 51\,\% of the \texttt{ES} and 98\,\% of the \texttt{FR} windows of 1,000 answers fire with nothing changed.
\item The majority country's test MdAPE: 17\,\% false alarms on windows of the test mix.
\item The weighted baseline without the margin: 7.8\,\% of the \texttt{ES} windows fire from the noise of its 593 test rows.
\item Market baselines for the coverage too: a new \texttt{evaluate} output, and twice the misses in small markets.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Only the two-sample ceiling keeps false alarms near 0.005 in every market: at most 0.0044 with the test values taken as the truth, 0.0081 for \texttt{ES} once its baseline's own noise counts.
It costs power where the baseline is thin: an \texttt{ES} window 20\,\% worse is missed in 47\,\% of windows.
The coverage floor is the ranges' promise to users, the same in every market.},
  ai = {Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI measured the options by resampling the test set, recommended the margin for the error alert and the nominal floor for coverage, and implemented them; the orchestrator checked the numbers against the results file.
Lukas took the recommendation unchanged.
Under his decision the orchestrator took the constant 3.55 over 4.00, which holds both rates at 0.005 but misses that \texttt{ES} window in 63\,\%.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.
Question (translated from German, paraphrased): ``\#306: how should ModelErrorHigh and ModelCoverageLow judge a window? Today both compare with the overall test value, so windows of only ES or only FR raise alerts without any degradation (ES 51\,\%, FR 98\,\% at 1,000 answers, against a level of 0.5\,\%).''
Orchestrator briefing (core, paraphrased): ``Give Lukas the options of \#306 (keep the overall baseline, a per-country baseline from segments.csv, a baseline weighted by the window's market mix) with their false-alarm and miss rates, measured with the resampling method of model\_alert\_thresholds.py, and what the rehearsal windows would have shown; implement nothing yet.''
Lukas answered: ``D for the error alert, coverage stays: ModelErrorHigh compares with the per-country test values, weighted by the window's country mix, plus a margin for their noise: false alarms near 0.5\,\% everywhere (at most 1.1\,\%), at the cost of missing ES +20\,\% in 47\,\% of windows. ModelCoverageLow stays at the 90\,\% promise; no new evaluate output. Window 18 of the rehearsal still fires the coverage alert.'' (translated from German)},
